response.justification: The candidate is an accomplished full-stack/web engineer with 15+ years of experience and a BS in Computer Science, which nominally satisfies the education-plus-experience threshold. However, the role requires deep hardware-domain expertise — SoC/IP modeling, AI accelerator performance architecture, GPU/SIMD/MIMD workload analysis, and hardware-software co-design — and the resume shows essentially none of this. Experience is concentrated in TypeScript/Node.js, D, web platforms, GIS, and mobile apps; the closest adjacent work (C/C++ components for LabWindows/CVI, low-latency D services, a wave-field-synthesis thesis) is systems-level at best, not silicon architecture. There is no evidence of deep learning training/inference optimization or chip-level performance modeling, so this is not a viable fit for a Principal Performance Architect.
strengths: 15+ years of broad, hands-on engineering across web, mobile, desktop, and embedded
Some low-level/performance work: C/C++ at National Instruments, low-latency D microservices at scale
Strong engineering discipline (TDD, CI/CD), open-source ownership, and public speaking/teaching
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture experience whatsoever
No AI accelerator, GPU, SIMD/MIMD, or deep-learning workload optimization background
Career trajectory is full-stack/product engineering, not principal-level hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware co-design expertise
No AI accelerator / GPU / DNN performance analysis experience
Extensive general software experience and systems-level C/C++ exposure
